# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura KS-698 NO GO round 1 (#882 @ `bd2b761a0`, tier 1)** — 2026-09-07 06:11→06:30 AEST, ~19 min; own `clone --shared` detached at `refs/qa/head` with `refs/qa/base` pinned to the LITERAL `306d0db92` (it re-confirmed the trap: the source's local `develop` is `ff5218867`, NOT the PR base), `merge-base --is-ancestor` asserted, `ls-remote` byte-identical at session OPEN and CLOSE | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It falsified the TIER RATING ITSELF, and the rating was Wednesday's.** F9: the brief's premise — *"the limiter FAILS OPEN on error (KS-616), so that key becomes effectively unlimited"* — breaks at two links. KS-616 is a **different limiter** (`api-gateway/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts`) that never consults this endpoint (`grep -n "fetch\|SECURITY\|http"` → NO MATCHES), and its fail-open was **already remediated at both SHAs, in the file's own past tense** (`:169` *"was: `next()`…"*, `:187` *"Degrade to the per-replica in-memory ceiling. CHOSEN"*), `git diff --stat` on that file EMPTY. Then a **caller census over 3552 files with THREE positive controls** (`keys/validate`→29 finding the real cross-service callers, `audit/logs`→2, `rate-limit`→308 proving the scan can match the domain) → **zero production consumers**; every `rate-limit/check` hit outside the service's own routes and docs is one schemathesis baseline line. Verdict: **availability, not a bypass — nothing became unlimited because nothing was limited by that Map.** **And it did not use that to dismiss the PR:** the defect is REAL and it reproduced it at the wire (base: the poisoned entry IS written and the next legitimate caller gets 500; head: 400, nothing written, next call 200), with a **plant-point control proving its probe could SEE the bug** — fixes 1+2 both removed → 4×500 and the poison returns; only fix 1 removed → fix 2 catches it with its own message, so each input-layer mechanism is independently load-bearing. **F1 MAJOR is the find:** the builder's extraction is real (neutering the product decision reds exactly the FIX 3 cell) **but it moved the fake one level up** — tampering the CALL SITE (`index.ts:1258` `usableRateLimitEntry(stored)` → `stored`) leaves **119/119 green with all six KS-698 cells passing**, and that tamper restores the original defect exactly. **F2 MAJOR:** the PR **introduces** an OpenAPI divergence (runtime gains `.max()`, `security.openapi.ts:492` and the published yaml keep min-and-no-max; `git diff --stat -- '*openapi*'` EMPTY) — and **the tool that FOUND KS-698 is spec-driven**, so a fuzzer will now generate legal-per-spec values the runtime rejects; `check:openapi` cannot see it because it regenerates the yaml from the untouched module. **F3/F4 MAJOR, pre-existing and live at BOTH SHAs:** any JWT, any role, any tenant can set `windowMs` on a key it does not own — **60× more permissive** or a **1440× lockout** — proved over real HTTP with the FAIL condition stated before the run. **F7 is the subtlest:** the builder's conclusion (fix 2 has no cell, its branch is unreachable) is TRUE and verified both ways — but **both halves of its stated REASON are false**, and it proved that by reaching fix 2's branch over the wire after removing fix 1, and by finding the supertest-free HTTP harness **three directory entries away already driving this route family**. **It corrected the builder's own remedy back at it:** fix 2's decision is the one decision in the PR that was not extracted.
